featured_reviews.name: Renu Chudamani
featured_reviews.review_text:
My mother recently had her cataract operation done at Ayush / Dr Agarwal’s eye clinic. Here’s an honest review of her experience.

1. Location: 5-stars - the location of the clinic is conveniently right at the beginning of postal colony, and although some road work was going on further down, it didn’t impact our ability to get in and out of the clinic with ease. The clinic is located on the first floor, even though there are 3 elevators, taking the stairs might be easier than the long wait for the elevator.
2. Facility: 4-stars: The entire place is kept very clean and tidy by a group of busy house keeping staff. The only gripe I had was the bathrooms did have an issue with water running from one of the hoses in the one stall. I also saw did see a cockroach (!!). However, I must say that when house cleaning was informed they took action right away.
3. Convenience: 5-stars: All in one clinic, you have your consultations, eye prescriptions, all ophthalmologist  related tests as well as two operating rooms make this truly a convenient experience. No need to run to another location to get anything.
4. Wait times: 4-5- stars: Varies, although we were seen within 15-20min for most of our appointments. On the day of the surgery we were seen almost right away.
5. Doctors: 5-stars: Dr Nita Shah is amazing, loved her calm reassuring demeanor and she was a realist, she didn’t try to give any false promises. She answered questions patiently even after a busy day of operations and seeing patients in the OPD. Stellar attitude, totally recommend this doctor!
6. Front-house/Triage Staff: 5-stars:  Ms Amrita went out of her way to help my mother, and comfort her about the procedure. She was patient with any questions, and helped square away questions about insurance, and what needed to be sent over. She even was able to help us offline with questions over WhatsApp. Really appreciated her help, and she was a big reason for why my mother wanted to get her cataract done at this location. Always smiling, fast and efficient, she truly is a star employee. Ms Snehanka was also a great help, she worked quickly to get us out of the hospital post surgery helping get prescriptions filled and ensuring payments are done on time.
7. Nurses: 4-stars: I think it’s here that the hospital can do some more work. The nurses are a little disorganized and although I think they’re all pretty competent it would be good for a ticketing system or something similar rather than someone calling out your name when your expected to move from station to station. On multiple occasions I saw that they mispronounced the patient names (no fault of theirs!!) but this led to some confusion. Also, there was some attitude from some of the nurses, I realize they had a heavy workload, so maybe something to look into with training and the hours they’re working.

Overall my mom had  great experience, pre and post op. Thank you!
P.S: One thing I did want to mention - they do have a screen up so you can watch your loved one’s cataract operation while it’s happening. Not for the faint of heart, and completely optional, it’s only through the window to the exclusive waiting room for patients that you can view this.

I had an extremely disappointing experience with Dr. Maithil that I feel compelled to share. During yesterday's appointment, he examined my eye and prescribed eye drops, suggesting the issue could be either severe dryness or early signs of infection. Given the uncertainty of the diagnosis, he insisted I return the following day for a mandatory follow-up examination to rule out infection.
I arrived at the clinic today at the exact time Dr. Maithil specified, only to be informed that he would not be coming in and that no other doctor would be available. This is completely unacceptable. When a doctor indicates that a next-day follow-up is medically necessary—particularly when infection is a possibility—the absolute minimum expectation is that the clinic contacts the patient if the doctor cannot make the appointment.
Not only was I left worried overnight about a potential infection, but I also rearranged my schedule to accommodate this "mandatory" appointment. The lack of communication shows a fundamental disregard for patients' time, health concerns, and peace of mind.
I hope Dr. Maithil and the clinic will implement better systems to ensure patients are notified of cancellations, especially when follow-up care has been deemed medically necessary.

featured_reviews.name: Priyamvada Mangal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had been experiencing vision issues and tried some alternative therapies, but my condition only worsened. I finally decided to respect my eyes and consulted an ophthalmologist in my area about three months ago. While she was competent with testing, she didn't seem confident and also suggested a re-LASIK procedure, which made me doubt her expertise since I had clearly stated I wasn't interested in surgery. When I recently went to LensKart to get spectacles made, they gave me a prescription number that was starkly different from what the previous doctor had provided.

My sister suggested a few nearby ophthalmologists, but when I researched their reviews, the top-rated ones appeared fake while the one-star reviews were horrific. When I discovered this clinic near me on Google, I had a good feeling about it and decided to visit. Although I had to wait for an hour, it was completely worth it. Dr. Maithil took a proper medical history, and when I casually mentioned having dry eyes, he conducted a thorough, separate examination for this condition instead of immediately prescribing a lens prescription. He explained that vision numbers fluctuate with dry eyes, so he's put me on a three-week dry eye treatment before rechecking and prescribing glasses, along with eye drops for three months.

I would highly recommend Dr. Maithil. Please avoid using unscientific drops and Ayurvedic treatments on your eyes—and I say this as a yoga teacher and someone who appreciates the science of Ayurveda when applied appropriately.  Additionally, please avoid taking prescriptions from opticians and optometrists for serious eye conditions. While they are qualified for basic vision testing and lens fitting, they cannot diagnose underlying medical conditions like dry eyes, glaucoma, or retinal issues that may be causing your vision problems. Only ophthalmologists have the medical training to identify and treat eye diseases, which could be the root cause of your vision changes.
